voice: a developer on the team who owns the payments API, writing to a teammate
brief: Phase: long multi-phase, idea to ship. Role: developer. Repo: a Node.js payments-style API (transfers, refunds) on node:http with middleware, a small response cache module and a request-id middleware. The ask: clients can send an `Idempotency-Key` header on POST requests so a retry returns the first response instead of doing the work twice; the same key with a different body is rejected; two requests with the same key at the same moment do not both run. Traps to plant (adapt, five or more): (1) body comparison must ignore JSON key order and whitespace; (2) server errors (5xx) must not be stored as the replayed answer, but 4xx validation answers may be; (3) the existing cache module takes TTL in seconds in one function and milliseconds in another; (4) keys are scoped per account, and docs/partners.md says one partner shares one account across several client ids; (5) keys expire after 24 hours, a stated number in docs, and the store has no expiry sweep. Decisions the design note must settle: key scope, in-flight handling, what is stored, expiry, which routes accept the header, rollout. The feature is built end to end: the request asks for a short design note, the feature with tests, a rollout plan and a release note.
